KEY MESSAGE 1...The parent low pressure has lifted to near Cape
Cod last evening with a trailing front/trough extending 
southward off the Eastern Seaboard. Another weaker low resides
along this boundary about 100nm SSE of Cape Hatteras which will
continue to push away from the area today. A mid-level shortwave
is lifting away from the area but abundant low level moisture 
remains across ENC and areas of light rain continues across the
area early this morning. Precip coverage is expected to wane
overnight but abundant low level moisture will remain in place
below 700mb and expect mostly cloudy skies to persist through
much of the day today. Some guidance continues to bring isolated
to widely scattered showers today but forcing will be limited
and additional rainfall amounts will be very light.

Seas are gradually subsiding along the coast with waves in the
surf zone below 8 ft and have allowed the High Surf Advisory to
expire. 

A strong but mainly dry cold front will push through the region
tonight with strong CAA ramping up after fropa with strong high
pressure building in from the north, which will finally bring a
much drier airmass into the region. Breezy conditions and 
cooler temps will be the story for Tuesday with wind gusts to 
around 20-25 mph inland and 30-40 mph along coastal sections 
Tuesday into Tuesday night. Temps will drop below normal Tuesday
with highs around 60.

KEY MESSAGE 2...We will continue to see increasing water levels
over the next few days as a result of the ongoing King Tide 
Cycle which will continue through the week, peaking during the 
middle of the week. This higher than normal astronomical tide 
cycle is slightly stronger than the one that occurred the last 
week of OCT. The tide levels may be exacerbated by a strong
north to northeasterly post frontal winds Tuesday and Tuesday
night and may see significant coastal flooding Wednesday into 
Thursday as a significant coastal storm is forecast to impact 
the region. 

The King tide cycle will be approaching its peak Tue/Wed which 
could act to pile up water especially soundside in the Pamlico 
sound and in the Neuse River and adjacent areas. This combination
could lead to some minor water level rises on Tue across both 
soundside and ocean side locations across the OBX and near the 
Neuse River. 

Another stronger low pressure system is expected to impact the 
area Wednesday into Thursday bring strong NE to E Gale Force 
winds, and some guidance is bringing a period of Storm Force
gusts ahead of the low Wednesday night. It is becoming 
increasingly likely that most tidal locations across ENC should 
expect elevated water levels with at least minor to moderate 
impacts with the potential for more significant impacts across 
the more vulnerable locations given he expected strength and 
duration of the winds. Interests along the coast should watch 
the forecast closely over the next few days for the potential 
for greater impacts, especially as it has to potential to impact
holiday travel.

KEY MESSAGE 3...
Yet another somewhat complex forecast is setting up across the 
area that looks to impact the holiday this week. In the upper 
levels a rather potent sub-tropical jet will remain in place 
though much of the week. An upper level trough currently noted 
along the west coast will track E'wards into the Plains as it 
rides along the aforementioned sub-tropical jet, while further 
to the north an upper level low will begin to dive SE'wards from
the Canadian Prairies and track towards the Ohio River Valley. 
Trough in the Plains will then track along the Gulf Coast taking
on a more negative tilt as it moves into the Southeastern CONUS
interacting with the upper level low that eventually settles 
into the Ohio River Valley around midweek. This will act to 
enhance divergence aloft near the Southeast coast Tue into Wed. 
At the mid levels, potent shortwave moves onshore the West 
Coast tonight and also pushes E towards the Gulf Coast, while at
the same time mid level low dives into the Ohio River Valley. 
These two mid level disturbances will also interact with each 
other and this interaction will go a long way in determining 
what the eventual evolution of the associated surface low track 
and strength will be. For now, confidence is increasing in a 
strong to potentially significant low impacting the region Wed 
into Thurs. 

Surface cyclogenesis develops near the Southeast Coast Tue 
night with this low then tracking NE while deepening. As it does
this, it will interact with the very strong high pressure 
centered to the north bringing the potential for strong winds, 
beach erosion, ocean overwash, and at least minor to 
moderate coastal flooding with the potential for more 
significant concerns given the most recent trends in guidance 
as this low will impact the area during the peak of the King 
Tide Cycle. Flooding due to heavy rain is also possible with the
